attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, written in his voice.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' conditional; 'likely' qualifies only the reason. Drafter drops 'begin to' before erode, slightly overstating it, but the contract keeps the original wording.

contract.note: Plain reading (affected free users leave, which reduces user growth) is ordinary. Requiring cohort-level causal evidence is fair, and aggregate growth is rightly not treated as disproof.

evidence.note: OpenAI status page, 2025-11-07: brief degradation for Free users. Shows the antecedent happened, but says nothing about later departures or growth.
OpenAI's June 2026 disclosure of aggregate adoption growth. Mixes tiers and does not isolate users exposed to outages, so it cannot settle the claim either way.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent is met: a dated Nov 2025 free-tier degradation. No evidence links that episode to departures or reduced growth, and aggregate adoption growth can't disprove it. No deadline and no causal finding, so the early-resolution rule isn't met. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the joint antecedent (OpenAI and CoreWeave both fail). The Core Scientific part is firm. The Crusoe part ('don't fancy chances') is hedged and would not be scored anyway.

contract.note: Defining failure as bankruptcy, insolvency, or cessation is ordinary. The contract correctly requires both antecedents before scoring and treats Crusoe as weaker.

evidence.note: CoreWeave press release, Oct 2026, showing it still operating. The antecedent is not shown to have occurred.
OpenAI partnership announcement, Oct 2026, showing it still operating. No failure documented.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast whose antecedent (both OpenAI and CoreWeave failing) is not documented. Both firms were operating in Oct 2026. An unmet or unknown antecedent is not scored. The Crusoe clause is hedged and also not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. 'As previously discussed' points back to his own earlier argument, not to someone else.

semantics.note: Captures both the load-bearing characterization and the exclusivity statement, with 'company' read as the ChatGPT product.

contract.note: Reading 'any meaningful userbase' as substantial recurring active use is ordinary and not stretched. Q1 2025 is a reasonable period. The load-bearing part has no threshold and stays untested.

evidence.note: Meta earnings call, 2025-01-29: over 700M monthly actives for Meta AI. This is a company disclosure, not an independent audit, but a figure that size is clearly a meaningful userbase.

reviews.rationale: The explicit claim that only ChatGPT had a meaningful userbase is contradicted by Meta's disclosed 700M+ monthly Meta AI users in the target period. That disclosure is self-reported and unaudited. The load-bearing characterization isn't tested by this evidence, but the conjunctive claim fails on its exclusivity part.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The 'already losing ground' observation is correctly separated from the preceding hypothetical about shifting compute.

contract.note: In a paragraph about model development, reading 'losing ground' as a narrowing capability lead is ordinary. It does not require OpenAI to have lost the lead.

evidence.note: Independent LMArena result, Jan 2025: DeepSeek-R1 tied for #1 with o1 on hard prompts.
DeepSeek's own v1 paper, Jan 2025, claims parity with o1-1217. Developer self-report, but backed up by e1.
Stanford AI Index summary of US–China gap closing in 2024. National aggregate from before the target period, so background only.
Epoch, Jan 31 2025: R1 roughly on par with o1, though DeepSeek is behind on software efficiency, which is a different measure. Fits a narrowing lead.

reviews.rationale: In Q1 2025, independent preference results (e1) and contemporaneous analysis (e4) put DeepSeek-R1 at about o1's level weeks after o1's release. That fits a narrowing OpenAI capability lead. The efficiency gap in e4 is a different measure and doesn't contradict this.
